9. After implementation, update the relevant project documentation, including:
   - README.md when user-facing behavior changes
   - docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
   - docs/DECISIONS.md
   - docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md
   - docs/EVIDENCE.md
   - docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md
   - any phase-specific setup or integration documentation
10. Mark the phase complete in the implementation plan only after its acceptance criteria pass.
11. Run all relevant verification. At minimum:
   - npm run typecheck
   - npm test
   - npm run build
   Run visual, security, budget, contract, migration, or integration tests when affected.
12. Review the final git diff for accidental files, secrets, debugging output, and unrelated changes.
13. Commit with the commit message specified by this phase.
14. Push the commit to origin/main. Never force-push.
15. If the push is rejected because origin/main advanced, fetch and rebase safely, resolve only scoped conflicts, rerun verification, and push normally.
16. Finish with:
   - implementation summary
   - changed files
   - documentation updated
   - tests and results
   - known limitations
   - commit hash
   - push result

Do not stop for ordinary implementation decisions. Stop only if there is a destructive conflict, missing required credential, irreconcilable remote conflict, or a decision that would materially change the product’s intended behavior.

## Upgrade Phase 5 — focused workshop and reorganized OpenCode controls

### Outcome

The workshop now presents one primary task at a time. The project outline, Project memory, and Activity & results are disclosure drawers; Activity & results is absent until an operation or check exists. The compact header carries the connection and selected model. OpenCode controls are split into Model & connection, a contextual permission request, and Advanced diagnostics; expensive session/usage data is loaded only when diagnostics are opened.

**Phase commit:** `refactor(ui): create a focused workshop experience`.

### Work units

| Unit | Outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| U5-1 focused layout | Single centered main document, compact titlebar/header, collapsible project outline, no permanent right rail | `src/web/workshop/WorkshopPage.tsx`, `src/web/styles.css` |
| U5-2 activity & results | Run Inspector renamed and reorganized into Progress, Changes, Checks; active/abandoned runs open it; no operation/evidence hides it | `src/web/components/RunInspector.tsx`, `tests/web.test.ts` |
| U5-3 technical disclosure | Native IDs, capability mappings, raw evidence, provider payloads, and transcript moved out of the primary view | `RunInspector` Technical details; `OpenCodePanel` Advanced diagnostics |
| U5-4 project memory | Decisions, user answers, assumptions, constraints, unresolved questions; add/correct flow; corrections supersede | `src/web/components/ProjectMemory.tsx`, `src/server/workflow/transitions.ts`, `src/server/app.ts`, `tests/memory.test.ts` |
| U5-5 OpenCode controls | Model & connection, contextual permission alert, lazy Advanced diagnostics; sessions/agents/commands/skills/MCP/LSP/formatters/revert/export/transcript stay advanced | `src/web/opencode-panel.tsx`, `src/web/api.ts` |
| U5-6 primary action | One primary action per stage; Approve becomes primary only for a current draft, otherwise Draft is primary | `src/web/workshop/WorkshopPage.tsx` |
| U5-7 accessibility and responsiveness | Native summary keyboard operation, stage-change focus, busy/permission live announcements, mobile drawer layout, reduced-motion-compatible styling | `WorkshopPage.tsx`, `styles.css`, `tests/visual/landing.spec.ts` |
| U5-8 budget and snapshots | Deliberate all-JS budget increase to 290 KiB; workshop, Activity & results, demo, and character snapshots refreshed | `scripts/check-budget.mjs`, `tests/visual/snapshots/` |
| U5-9 documentation | README, architecture, decisions, UX, operations, evidence, release notes, changelog, implementation plan | canonical documentation set |

### Acceptance status

- [x] The main task is understandable without opening advanced controls.
- [x] Empty technical panels no longer occupy permanent screen space; Activity & results is absent with no operation/evidence.
- [x] Permission requests render as a contextual alert outside collapsed diagnostics and remain actionable in Model & connection/Advanced diagnostics.
- [x] Project memory is useful and editable; corrections preserve superseded history and never change an approval or draft.
- [x] One primary action is visible per stage; approval remains separate from revision acceptance.
- [x] Drawers work with keyboard and screen-reader semantics; stage changes move focus to the main task and announce busy/permission state.
- [x] Advanced diagnostics load only when opened; sessions, agents, commands, skills, MCP, LSP, formatters, low-level revert, export, and raw transcripts stay out of the normal flow.
- [x] Schema v7 is unchanged; the memory edit route uses the existing status/supersedesId fields.
- [x] Final typecheck, 184 tests, build, 290 KiB all-JS budget, 19 visual tests, and diff/security review pass.

content.text:
Implement Phase 6: replace the inconsistent demo, rewrite the landing page, and make the hackathon theme part of the product story.

Objectives:

- Use one canonical sample dataset.
- Replace the generic example with a coherent abandoned-project revival.
- Simplify landing-page copy and visual hierarchy.
- Make the OpenCode relationship understandable.

Implementation requirements:

1. Create one canonical demo fixture used by:
   - guided demo;
   - landing preview;
   - visual tests;
   - screenshots;
   - evidence examples.
2. Remove contradictory PASS/FAIL states from separate fixture sources.
3. Replace the current example with a small, self-contained abandoned open-source project:
   - clear original problem;
   - Oracle discovery;
   - Architect plan;
   - bounded Maker change;
   - relevant test;
   - honest Witness evidence.
4. Make every section and generated artifact consistent with the same example.
5. Rewrite technical/jargon-heavy demo text in plain language.
6. Keep technical fixture disclosures available, but place them under details.
7. Rebuild the landing page around:
   - Hero
   - Four-stage workflow
   - Sample project
   - Why OpenCode
   - Local setup and privacy
   - FAQ/final CTA
8. Keep Try the example as the primary CTA.
9. Remove the duplicate Watch guided flow action.
10. Keep Run locally as a secondary action.
11. Replace technical hero facts with user outcomes:
    - Clarify the idea
    - Approve the plan
    - Build with OpenCode
    - Verify the result
12. Rewrite “OpenCode is the engine” in direct language.
13. Rename or replace:
    - Deterministic walkthrough
    - OpenCode controls and evidence
    - Hosted demo or private hosted
    - Full local mode
14. Remove the idea-to-tool recommendation unless it becomes genuinely interactive and capability-driven.
15. Replace the generic hero image with a bespoke visual aligned with the four spirits and abandoned-project workshop concept. If creating a raster illustration, use the available image-generation skill and store an optimized web asset with appropriate responsive variants.
16. Reduce oversized typography, excess glass cards, pills, outlines, glows, and monospace labels.
17. Add fixture-consistency and visual-regression tests.

Acceptance criteria:

- Landing and demo always report the same sample outcome.
- The sample tells one coherent story from idea through evidence.
- The hackathon theme is functional rather than cosmetic.
- The page has one obvious primary CTA.
- Desktop and mobile layouts have intentional scale and spacing.

42: | Shared components | `RunInspector`, `SpiritCharacter`, `SpiritStageTabs`, `StatusChip`, `Brand` |
43: 
44: The fixture contains the input idea, Oracle clarification, approved product summary, eight Architect sections, two revisions, Maker authorization, normalized operations, a representative diff, verification output, Witness findings, submission readiness, and next actions. Section hashes are real SHA-256 hashes of the fixed content and are recomputed by the test.
45: 
46: The fixture is browser-safe: it imports no server, filesystem, network, provider, or OpenCode module. `tests/demo.test.ts` also reads the source to assert that it has no `fetch`, `/api/`, `node:`, `Date.now`, `Math.random`, or `process.env` use.
47: 
48: ## Playback
49: 
50: | Control | Behavior |
51: |---|---|
52: | Play / Pause | Starts or stops deterministic auto-advance |
53: | Previous / Next step | Moves one beat and pauses |
54: | Replay | Returns to beat 1 and plays |
55: | Reset | Returns to beat 1, paused, and clears tab inspection |
56: | Spirit tabs | Inspect Oracle, Architect, Maker, or Witness at any time; inspection pauses playback |
57: | 90s mode | Enters the screen-recording presentation path |
58: 
59: Normal playback holds each of the 10 beats for 7 seconds. Presentation mode holds each beat for 9 seconds, for exactly 90 seconds. Presentation mode is optional; normal interactive use remains available. `?presentation=1` is the route-refresh state for presentation mode.
60: 
61: The demo uses `setTimeout` only for playback. It makes no network request, inference call, provider call, or mutation request. The Playwright test records requests during playback and asserts that no `/api/` or provider URL is contacted.
62: 
63: ## Reset behavior
64: 
65: Reset is a pure reducer transition in `src/web/demo/playback.ts`. It changes only:
66: 
67: - the demo beat index;
68: - the playing/paused flag;
69: - the inspected spirit tab;
70: - the completed flag.
71: 
72: It cannot call `/api/*`, cannot change a live project snapshot, cannot start or stop an OpenCode session, and cannot clear live state. In hosted-demo mode the server independently rejects every non-GET `/api/*` request with `DEMO_READ_ONLY`, so a browser cannot reach a live mutation even if the UI were bypassed.
73: 
74: ## Live-versus-simulated disclosure
75: 
76: | Claim | Demo behavior |
77: |---|---|
78: | “This is live inference” | **Prohibited.** The page says no provider call or model quota is used. |
79: | “The check passed” | Allowed only with the label “prerecorded demo fixture”; the live session is shown as `NOT_RUN`. |
80: | “This is the visitor's repository” | **Prohibited.** The workspace is `demo://campus-umbrella-relay`. |
81: | “This is a submitted hackathon entry” | **Prohibited.** The Witness readiness statement says it is not a submission. |
82: | “Reset is safe for live state” | Allowed with the exact scope: reset changes only the demo fixture. |
83: 
84: Every simulated operation, evidence row, diff, and finding carries a visible `Demo data` chip or a fixture source label. Activity & results receives the same operation/evidence/capability shapes as the live workshop.
85: 
86: ## Phase 9 evidence boundary
87: 
88: - The fixture, reset isolation, schema drift, 90-second timing, tab inspection, and no-network behavior are covered by `tests/demo.test.ts` and `tests/visual/demo.spec.ts`.
89: - The hosted demo was smoke-tested locally: fixture project, no session token, `DEMO_READ_ONLY` mutation, no engine, and a rendered `/demo`.
90: - The last real native inference recorded in this repository remains the Experience-phase umbrella-relay run, which produced a real Maker diff and a failing `node --test`; Witness recorded the failure. Phase 9 did not repeat live inference.
91: - No video file, public hosted URL, published article, or submission receipt exists. Do not claim one.
92: 
93: ## Exact claims
94: 
95: Approved:
96: 
97: - “The guided example is a deterministic fixture.”
98: - “OpenCode supplies the agent loop, model access, native tools, permissions, and sessions.”
99: - “The example shows the same Activity & results contract used by the live workshop.”
100: - “The fixture check passes; the live native session is not run.”
101: - “Reset affects only the demo fixture.”
102: - “Run live with OpenCode for a real native session.”
103: - “The hosted demo is read-only and has no repository, provider key, or user-specific storage.”
104: 
105: Not approved:
106: 
107: - “Live inference” or “real OpenCode run” around the fixture.
108: - “Reads your repository from the hosted page.”
109: - “Guaranteed working build.”
110: - “Autonomous end-to-end submission.”
111: - Any testimonial, user count, award, sponsor endorsement, performance metric, deployment result, or competition result that has not been observed.
112: 
113: ## 90-second presentation path
114: 
115: The presentation mode is 10 beats × 9 seconds. A recording can follow this beat map:
116: 
117: | Time | Beat | What to show |
118: |---|---|---|
119: | 0–9s | Problem | The group-chat umbrella problem and the unfinished idea |
120: | 9–18s | Oracle | Clarification, open questions, explicit product approval |
121: | 18–27s | Architect | One section drafted; revision makes the old approval stale |
122: | 27–36s | Approval | Exact-version approval and the eight-section plan |
123: | 36–45s | Scope | Separate Maker authorization; permission boundary |
124: | 45–54s | Run | Maker progress: queued → running → succeeded (fixture replay) |
125: | 54–63s | Diff | Representative diff with the source label visible |
126: | 63–72s | Check | Deterministic `node --test` output and the `NOT_RUN` live session |
127: | 72–81s | Witness | Pass, limitations, readiness, and next actions |
128: | 81–90s | Next step | Clean exit to local setup or live OpenCode |
129: 
130: Narration should name the four spirits, explain that the run is a prerecorded fixture, and end with “run live with OpenCode for a native session.”
131: 
132: ## Screenshots and video beats
133: 
134: Canonical Playwright captures:
135: 
136: | File | Shows |
137: |---|---|
138: | `tests/visual/snapshots/demo-guided-wide.png` | Wide guided example: intro, honesty panel, playback controls |
139: | `tests/visual/snapshots/demo-guided-narrow.png` | 390px guided example without horizontal overflow |
140: | `tests/visual/snapshots/demo-presentation-wide.png` | 90-second presentation mode |
141: | `tests/visual/snapshots/run-inspector.png` | Activity & results at the check beat, including fixture PASS and live `NOT_RUN` (filename retained for history) |
142: | `tests/visual/snapshots/recovery-unknown.png` | Unknown native run and reconcile action |
143: | `tests/visual/snapshots/landing-wide.png` | Landing page with the three distinct demo/live actions |
144: | `tests/visual/snapshots/landing-narrow.png` | Narrow landing page |
145: | `tests/visual/snapshots/workshop-wide.png` | Live workshop structure |
146: | `tests/visual/snapshots/onboarding-wide.png` | OpenCode connection/discovery |
147: | `tests/visual/snapshots/spirit-*.png` | Character states |
148: 
149: Video rules:
150: 
151: - Keep the fixture label and `NOT_RUN` visible when showing evidence.
152: - Do not speed-edit the fixture into a live run.
153: - Do not add fake terminal output, dashboards, success badges, or deployment results.
154: - If a live recording fails, show the failure and say so.
155: - Use the actual viewport; do not stretch narrow screenshots.
156: 
157: ## Regenerating snapshots
158: 
159: ```bash
160: npm run build
161: npm run test:visual
162: ```
163: 
164: After a deliberate visual change:
165: 
166: ```bash
167: npx playwright test --update-snapshots
168: ```
169: 
170: Review every changed image before committing. A snapshot change is a UI decision, not an automatic approval.
171: 
172: ## Clean exit
173: 
174: The guided example ends with two honest exits:
175: 
176: - **Run live with OpenCode** → `/workshop`, which shows the real connection/discovery flow.
177: - **Local setup** → `/#local-setup`, which links to the tested commands in `docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md`.
178: 
179: The hosted demo also rejects mutation routes, so “Run live” is an explicit path to a local or private deployment rather than an implied capability of the public sample.

Why OpenCode

OpenCode does the coding. This workshop does the deciding.

OpenCode is the open-source engine. It owns model access, tools, permissions, sessions, and execution. Unfinished Business gives that work a four-stage workshop: clarify, approve, build, and verify. Approving a plan here never overrides a tool denial inside OpenCode.

1: # Unfinished Business
2: 
3: **Turn unfinished ideas into hackathon-ready builds.**
4: 
5: Unfinished Business is an OpenCode-powered hackathon project builder. Four friendly spirits guide one idea through a clear proposal, an approved plan, a real bounded build, and evidence you can defend.
6: 
7: ![Ghostlight Hacker Workshop landing page](tests/visual/snapshots/landing-wide.png)
8: 
9: ## What it is
10: 
11: - A **landing page** at `/` that explains the product, the four roles, OpenCode's role, and the three honest usage paths.
12: - A **guided deterministic example** at `/demo`: a versioned Campus Umbrella Relay fixture with Play/Pause, step, replay, reset, four inspectable spirit tabs, a representative diff and check, Witness findings, and an optional 90-second presentation mode at `/demo?presentation=1`. It does not call a model or read a repository.
13: - The **real workshop** at `/workshop`, which connects to a local OpenCode server and records what actually happened.
14: - A **first-run connection and discovery flow** that checks a supported OpenCode server, lists the models/providers/agents it actually reports, and lets the builder choose a model and reported reasoning variant. Provider API keys stay inside OpenCode.
15: - A **read-only hosted demo** and a **private hosted** mode. Neither reaches into a visitor's local repository.
16: - A versioned **schema v7** contract for explicit project sources, field-level Oracle intake answers, structured facts/decisions/assumptions with editable superseding corrections, structured proposals, reviewable candidate section revisions, model preferences, provider errors, and recoverable operations. Explicit v1–v6 migrations keep older projects usable.
17: - **Reviewable Architect revisions**: every section has a content contract; a change request generates a candidate with a summary and complete Markdown draft. The user inspects a unified or side-by-side diff, then accepts, requests another revision, or discards. Only an accepted candidate replaces the current draft, and approval remains a separate exact-version action.
18: - **Focused workshop**: one primary task at a time, a collapsible project outline, a contextual Activity & results drawer, an editable Project memory drawer, and a compact model/connection header. Empty technical panels no longer occupy permanent space.
19: - **Activity & results**: the former Run Inspector is organized into Progress, Changes, and Checks. Native IDs, capability mappings, raw evidence, provider payloads, and the transcript stay under Technical details or Advanced diagnostics.
20: - **Editable project memory**: decisions, user answers, assumptions, constraints, and unresolved questions are visible in one place. A correction supersedes the prior entry without changing an approval, section draft, Maker scope, or native run.
21: - **Focused, multi-turn Oracle discovery**: every fresh project chooses new work, a validated local repository, a credential-free remote repository import, or saved work before discovery. Oracle asks at most three explained questions per turn and proposes only after essential intake is known or the user explicitly accepts stated assumptions.
22: - **Observable, cancellable, recoverable runs**: every Oracle, Architect, Maker, and Witness run is a persisted asynchronous operation with live progress phases, elapsed time, and Continue waiting / Reconcile / Open in OpenCode / Cancel / Retry / Mark abandoned controls in Activity & results. A timed-out or restarted run never permanently blocks the project; reconciliation retrieves and validates the actual late response or diff and applies it exactly once.
23: 
24: OpenCode supplies the agent loop, model access, native tools, permissions, execution, interruption, and native sessions. Unfinished Business adds the four-stage workshop, exact-version approvals, dependency invalidation, evidence views, the onboarding/discovery flow, and the Ghostlight interface. It does **not** ship a second coding harness or a general command executor.
25: 
26: | Spirit | Role |
27: |---|---|
28: | Oracle | Choose the project source, collect structured answers over focused turns, and prepare a fact/decision/assumption-aware proposal |
29: | Architect | Draft one planning section and wait for approval of that exact version |
30: | Maker | Perform an approved, bounded native edit through OpenCode |
31: | Witness | Inspect evidence in a fresh session and prepare honest review drafts |
32: 
33: ## Three honest usage paths
34: 
35: **Hosted demo** — `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=hosted-demo`. A public, deterministic sample. It has no OpenCode process, provider credentials, session token, visitor persistence, or repository access. Every non-GET `/api/*` request returns `403 DEMO_READ_ONLY`.
36: 
37: **Private hosted** — `REDACTED`. A password-protected Render or self-hosted instance with a private disk and a loopback OpenCode child. Maker edits the server's isolated demo workspace. A hosted browser cannot edit a visitor's machine.
38: 
39: **Full local mode** — `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=local` (default). The browser app, local API, and pinned OpenCode server run on the builder's machine over loopback. Oracle source onboarding validates local directories and can import a public HTTPS repository into an app-managed workspace after explicit confirmation. Maker's edit remains bounded to the isolated demo workspace; selecting a source does not authorize implementation in that repository.
40: 
41: The landing page exposes three distinct actions: **Try the example** (`/demo`), **Watch the guided workflow** (`/demo?presentation=1`), and **Run live with OpenCode** (`/workshop`). The example is always labeled as a prerecorded fixture; the live native session remains `NOT_RUN`.
42: 
43: Models are discovered from OpenCode rather than assumed. New projects default to **All accessible models**, so any model OpenCode reports as available can be selected. A project can deliberately switch to **Free and local only**, which blocks paid and unknown-price remote models. Paid or unknown-price remote models require an explicit first-use confirmation; the app never silently substitutes a model or makes a paid request without that confirmation. An optional USD session spending limit can be set, and the deployment can impose a stricter `UB_MAX_SESSION_COST_USD` ceiling. Cost is checked against the value OpenCode reports; an unknown-price provider may report it only after a request.

112: ## Status and limitations
113: 
114: The prior release phases remain integrated. Upgrade Phase 5 focuses the workshop: one main task, a collapsible outline, contextual Activity & results, editable Project memory, a compact model/connection header, and lazy Advanced diagnostics. The Activity view separates Progress, Changes, and Checks; technical references live under Technical details. Upgrade Phase 4 remains the reviewable-revision model: section contracts, explicit accept/reject, safe Markdown, responsive diffs, and separate approval. Schema v7 is unchanged.
115: 
116: Known limitations:
117: 
118: - The application is a trusted single-project tool, not a multi-tenant sandbox. Remote imports are public HTTPS clones into a managed local directory; private/authenticated repositories, shared-host isolation, arbitrary Maker access to selected repositories, and remote browser-to-local pairing remain deferred.
119: - Maker edits only `UB_DATA_DIR/demo-workspace`; the Node check is not an OS sandbox.
120: - Generated section review supports a deliberately small, safe Markdown subset (headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, links, tables, and code), not full CommonMark or raw HTML. Contract validation checks structure and topic coverage, not prose quality.
121: - Model availability, pricing, quota, training terms, and billing are controlled by OpenCode/provider. The spending limit only checks cost OpenCode reports after a session; unknown-price providers may bill before that value is visible.
122: - The workspace privacy preference records intent; the app cannot attest every provider's training/retention contract. Provider rejections that mention training/data policy are explained as `PROVIDER_DATA_POLICY`.
123: - Advanced diagnostics load only when opened. Permission polling is best-effort; a pending request remains visible in Activity & results and the contextual permission alert, but a provider-side change can lag by one refresh interval.
124: - Backboard is not integrated and no partner category is claimed for installation alone. Sentry is configured but live release/source-map/trace verification requires authorized credentials and a deployment.
125: - No public hosted URL, recorded video, published article, or submission is asserted by this repository.
126: - A real recorded demonstration and final submission packaging remain separate acceptance work.

# Architecture — Unfinished Business

**Status:** Upgrade Phase 5 (focused workshop and reorganized OpenCode controls) implemented on the verified Phase 4 baseline.
**Owner:** Engineering.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01 against the Phase 5 verification matrix recorded in `docs/EVIDENCE.md`.

## 1. System shape

```text
Browser
  ├─ /            landing page (eager)
  ├─ /demo        deterministic walkthrough (lazy chunk)
  └─ /workshop    real workshop (lazy chunk)
        │
        │ same-origin fetch /api/*
        │ Basic Auth in hosted modes; x-ub-session-token on protected API routes
        ▼
Hono server (src/server/app.ts)
  ├─ /api/health                 public, minimal
  ├─ /api/mode                   public mode descriptor
  ├─ /api/session                token issue (loopback/local, Basic Auth/private)
  ├─ /api/runtime                effective limits/retention
  ├─ /api/engine                 connection/engine summary
  ├─ /api/connection*            check, configure (local only), reset
  ├─ /api/opencode/*             discovery, project-owned sessions, permissions, usage
  ├─ /api/engine/selection       persist a discovered model allowed by project policy
  ├─ /api/model-preferences      access mode, privacy preference, optional spending limit
  ├─ /api/project, /api/export   snapshot/approved plan; workspace paths omitted
  ├─ /api/project/source*        select source; explicitly confirm managed remote import
  ├─ /api/events                 authenticated bounded SSE snapshots
---
- the run coordinator records progress phases through safe polling (`session.get`, `message.list`, `permission.request.list`) plus directed callbacks from the native guide; prompts, raw model text, and unvalidated JSON are never persisted as progress;
- a timeout, disconnect, or restart leaves the operation `ABANDONED` with an `AWAITING_RECONCILIATION` marker and its native session reference; it blocks new runs until reconciled but never permanently blocks the project;
- reconciliation observes the native outcome, retrieves the actual late reply or diff through fresh reads, validates it with the same schemas as live completions, and applies it at most once (`appliedAt` plus the idempotent action record); an idle session alone is never success;
- `POST /api/runs/:id/retry` starts a new Maker operation with `retryOf` lineage after a confirmed `FAILED` outcome; uncertain runs must be reconciled first;
- `POST /api/runs/:id/abandon` records a user decision on an outstanding operation when no in-process runner is active;
- startup marks in-flight work `ABANDONED` with a recovery marker; reconciliation reads native state and never replays automatically;
- evidence records an observed native result/fingerprint; a missing result is an empty state.

`AtomicProjectStore` acquires a cross-process lock, writes a private temp file, fsyncs, renames, keeps `.previous` and rolling `backups/`, quarantines corrupt current files, and prunes bounded retention. A corrupt current with no valid previous returns `STATE_CORRUPT`; it never silently resets.

## 8. Demo fixture boundaries

The deterministic demo is a browser-bundled fixture, not a server response and not a parallel UI:

```text
src/shared/workflow.ts   production Zod schemas + types
        │
        ├─ src/server/workflow/model.ts  hashing, migration, persistence helpers
        ├─ src/shared/demo.ts            versioned fixture + playback beats
        └─ src/web/demo/DemoPage.tsx     playback + shared components
                    │
                    ├─ RunInspector
                    ├─ SpiritStageTabs (inspect variant)
                    ├─ SpiritCharacter / StatusChip / Brand
                    └─ pure playback reducer (no API calls)
```

`src/shared/demo.ts` has no `node:`, `fetch`, `process.env`, `Date.now`, or `Math.random`. Tests parse the fixture with the production schemas and recompute section hashes. Every fixture result is labeled; the live session remains `NOT_RUN`.

In `hosted-demo` mode the server independently returns the fixture from `/api/project` and `/api/export`, returns a read-only connection status, rejects `/api/session` and every non-GET `/api/*` request, and never constructs an OpenCode connection.

## 9. Trust boundaries and residual risks

| Boundary | Enforced controls |
|---|---|
| Browser → app | Host/Origin/CSRF policy, Basic Auth in hosted modes, constant-time session token, JSON content type, request-size cap, rate/concurrency limits |
| App → disk | Canonical roots, traversal/symlink rejection, regular-file checks, `0700` directories, `0600` files, lock, fsync, previous snapshot, backups, quarantine |
| App → OpenCode | URL syntax, loopback default, HTTPS and explicit host allowlist for remote, optional port allowlist, DNS/IP classification, redirect refusal, timeout, response cap, version/auth/model readiness |
| App → repository source | Canonical local-directory policy; public HTTPS-only remote URL; embedded-credential rejection; managed workspace; explicit confirmation before import; no Maker write authority in Phase 3; paths omitted from browser/model |
| OpenCode → provider | Native credentials, permissions, sessions; the app never reads provider keys |
| App → Sentry | Collection disabled, event/breadcrumb scrubbing, metadata-only spans, no prompts/tool args/results/local paths |

| D4-22 | Preserve the remote onboarding commit and integrate it rather than overwrite it | Push the Phase 4 commit over the remote or discard onboarding | The remote work is user work and adds required connection functionality | Both histories preserved through integration; 111 tests pass in the Phase 9 candidate |

## Phase 7 — guided demo

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D7-01 | Use a versioned browser-bundled fixture | Server endpoint; live model call; video only | Deterministic playback must work without network, provider, or credentials | `src/shared/demo.ts`; no `/api/` call from `/demo` |
| D7-02 | Extract browser-safe workflow schemas to `src/shared/workflow.ts` | Duplicate schemas in the demo | One production contract; drift fails a test | Server model re-exports the shared schemas; fixture is parsed by `projectSchema` |

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D8-01 | Use one canonical `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (`local`, `hosted-demo`, `private-hosted`) | Keep parallel `UB_MODE` values | Two mode dialects caused contradictory docs and startup behavior | Legacy alias accepted; `hosted-private` and `private-hosted` map to the same mode |
| D8-02 | Make hosted-demo public and read-only, not password-protected | Reuse the private Basic Auth path for the demo | The demo contains no user data, secret, engine, or mutation; requiring credentials would make the judge path worse | No token, no OpenCode, every non-GET `/api/*` → `DEMO_READ_ONLY` |
| D8-03 | Require session token on protected API reads as well as writes | Token only on mutations | State, connection, discovery, usage, and exports can contain project/native metadata | Browser client obtains the token once; manual API checks need the header |
| D8-04 | Reject paid or unpriced remote models at selection | Accept any discovered model and rely on cost afterward | The release promises no paid fallback | Superseded for new projects by U1-01; migrated projects retain this as the default policy |

| D8-06 | Refuse to mark cancellation when native interruption fails | Mark CANCELLED anyway | Native effects may continue | Explicit `CANCEL_UNAVAILABLE`; reconcile instead |
| D8-07 | Use a lock, fsync, backups, quarantine, and state v2 | Single overwrite or reset-on-corrupt | Approvals and evidence must survive crashes | Recovery is visible; both-corrupt state refuses reset |

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |

| U0-01 | Introduce schema v3 as an additive persisted contract | Mutate v2 in place; defer schema work until features ship | Later phases need stable fields without risking existing approvals/evidence | Explicit v1/v2 readers and one canonical v3 writer |

# Demo and submission guidance

**Status:** Guided sample and first-release evidence complete. A real recorded video, published article, deployment, and submission remain pending explicit authorization.
**Owner:** Demo/submission.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01 (20 visual/accessibility tests; 185 unit/integration/component tests).

## Two different demos

| Demo | What it is | What it proves |
|---|---|---|
| Guided sample (`/demo`) | One versioned Driftwatch fixture played through the real interface components | Interface states, approval language, permission boundaries, evidence wording, recovery, and reset isolation |
| Real workshop (`/workshop`) | The four-stage workflow connected to a local OpenCode server | Actual native sessions, observed tool results, real failures and success |

Never present the guided sample as live inference. Never use a sample screenshot to claim a real build passed. The sample page and its fixture are deliberately separate from live project data.

## Scenario: Driftwatch

The sample revives a small abandoned open-source issue-triage CLI:

1. Driftwatch reads a local `issues.json` export and prints issues that have gone quiet.
2. The copied project parses the export, but it still counts closed issues and measures age from the creation date instead of the latest activity.
3. The Oracle clarifies one local export, a 90-day window, closed issues skipped, and age measured from the latest activity date.
4. The Architect approves eight sections; a revision narrows the first release and makes the old approval stale.
5. Maker receives a separate scope for two files in `demo-workspace/`.
6. One bounded change skips closed issues, measures the latest activity, keeps the report shape stable, and adds a behavioural test.
7. A recorded `node --test` check reports 4 passed, 0 failed.
8. Witness separates the recorded pass from the missing live proof and states the next honest step.

No real repository, maintainer, sponsor, user, metric, deployment, account, or competition result is depicted. The sample is an original story about a hackathon team reviving abandoned open-source work, not a claim about a real project.

## Fixture and provenance

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Fixture module | `src/shared/demo.ts` |
| Fixture version | `driftwatch@1` |
| Data mode | `demo` |
| Source label | `Recorded sample — not a live OpenCode session` |
| Production contract | `src/shared/workflow.ts` (`projectSchema`, operation/evidence/capability schemas) |
| Drift test | `tests/demo.test.ts` |
| Landing consistency | `tests/web.test.ts`; `tests/visual/landing.spec.ts` |
| Playback state | `src/web/demo/playback.ts` |
| UI | `src/web/demo/DemoPage.tsx`, `src/web/landing/DemoTeaser.tsx` |
| Shared components | `RunInspector`, `SpiritCharacter`, `SpiritStageTabs`, `StatusChip`, `Brand` |

The fixture contains the input idea, Oracle clarification, approved product summary, eight Architect sections, two revisions, Maker authorization, normalized operations, a representative diff, verification output, Witness findings, submission readiness, and next actions. Section hashes are real SHA-256 hashes of the fixed content and are recomputed by the test.

The fixture is browser-safe: it imports no server, filesystem, network, provider, or OpenCode module. `tests/demo.test.ts` also reads the source to assert that it has no `fetch`, `/api/`, `node:`, `Date.now`, `Math.random`, or `process.env` use.

**One canonical source.** `src/web/content/landing.ts` holds copy and configuration only. The landing preview (`demoPreviewSteps`), the evidence view, and the guided sample all read the same fixture. There is no second landing operation/evidence list and no contradictory PASS/FAIL state.

## Playback

| Control | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Play / Pause | Starts or stops deterministic auto-advance |
| Previous / Next step | Moves one beat and pauses |
| Replay | Returns to beat 1 and plays |
| Reset | Returns to beat 1, paused, and clears tab inspection |
| Spirit tabs | Inspect Oracle, Architect, Maker, or Witness at any time; inspection pauses playback |
| 90s mode | Enters the screen-recording presentation path |

Normal playback holds each of the 10 beats for 7 seconds. Presentation mode holds each beat for 9 seconds, for exactly 90 seconds. Presentation mode is optional; normal interactive use remains available. `?presentation=1` is the route-refresh state for presentation mode.

The sample uses `setTimeout` only for playback. It makes no network request, inference call, provider call, or mutation request. The Playwright test records requests during playback and asserts that no `/api/` or provider URL is contacted.

## Reset behavior

Reset is a pure reducer transition in `src/web/demo/playback.ts`. It changes only:

- the sample beat index;
- the playing/paused flag;
- the inspected spirit tab;
- the completed flag.

It cannot call `/api/*`, cannot change a live project snapshot, cannot start or stop an OpenCode session, and cannot clear live state. In hosted-sample mode the server independently rejects every non-GET `/api/*` request with `DEMO_READ_ONLY`, so a browser cannot reach a live mutation even if the UI were bypassed.

## Live-versus-recorded disclosure

| Claim | Sample behavior |
|---|---|
| “This is live inference” | **Prohibited.** The page says no provider call or model quota is used. |
| “The check passed” | Allowed only with the label “recorded sample”; the live session is shown as `NOT_RUN`. |
| “This is the visitor's repository” | **Prohibited.** The workspace is `demo://driftwatch`. |
| “This is a submitted hackathon entry” | **Prohibited.** The Witness readiness statement says it is not a submission. |
| “Reset is safe for live state” | Allowed with the exact scope: reset changes only the sample. |

Every simulated operation, evidence row, diff, and finding carries a visible `Sample data` chip or a recorded-sample source label. Activity & results receives the same operation/evidence/capability shapes as the live workshop. Provenance, fixture version, technical caveats, and the evidence inspector sit under `<details>` so the main story stays plain-language.

## Evidence boundary

- The fixture, reset isolation, schema drift, 90-second timing, tab inspection, no-network behavior, and canonical landing/demo consistency are covered by `tests/demo.test.ts`, `tests/web.test.ts`, and `tests/visual/`.
- The hosted sample was smoke-tested locally: fixture project, no session token, `DEMO_READ_ONLY` mutation, no engine, and a rendered `/demo`.
- The last real native inference recorded in this repository remains the Experience-phase umbrella-relay run, which produced a real Maker diff and a failing `node --test`; Witness recorded the failure. Phase 9 did not repeat live inference. Phase 6 changed the public sample scenario but did not use a live provider call.
- No video file, public hosted URL, published article, or submission receipt exists. Do not claim one.

## Exact claims

Approved:

- “The guided sample is a recorded fixture.”
- “OpenCode supplies the agent loop, model access, native tools, permissions, and sessions.”
- “Unfinished Business adds the four-stage workshop, exact-version approvals, dependency invalidation, and an evidence ledger.”
- “The sample shows the same Activity & results contract used by the live workshop.”
- “The recorded check passes; the live native session is not run.”
- “Reset affects only the sample.”
- “Run locally with OpenCode for a real native session.”
- “The hosted sample is read-only and has no repository, provider key, or user-specific storage.”

Not approved:

- “Live inference” or “real OpenCode run” around the recorded sample.
- “Reads your repository from the hosted page.”
- “Guaranteed working build.”
- “Autonomous end-to-end submission.”
- Any testimonial, user count, award, sponsor endorsement, performance metric, deployment result, or competition result that has not been observed.

## 90-second presentation path

The presentation mode is 10 beats × 9 seconds. A recording can follow this beat map:

| Time | Beat | What to show |
|---|---|---|
| 0–9s | Problem | The abandoned Driftwatch CLI and the untrustworthy stale-issue report |
| 9–18s | Oracle | Clarification, open questions, explicit product approval |
| 18–27s | Architect | One section drafted; revision makes the old approval stale |
| 27–36s | Approval | Exact-version approval and the eight-section plan |
| 36–45s | Scope | Separate Maker authorization; permission boundary |
| 45–54s | Run | Maker progress: queued → running → succeeded (recorded replay) |
| 54–63s | Diff | Representative diff with the source label visible |
| 63–72s | Check | Recorded `node --test` output and the `NOT_RUN` live session |
| 72–81s | Witness | Pass, limitations, readiness, and next actions |
| 81–90s | Next step | Clean exit to local setup or live OpenCode |

Narration should name the four spirits, explain that the run is a recorded sample, and end with “run locally with OpenCode for a native session.”

## Screenshots and video beats

Canonical Playwright captures:

| File | Shows |
|---|---|
| `tests/visual/snapshots/demo-guided-wide.png` | Wide guided sample: intro, sample details, playback controls |
| `tests/visual/snapshots/demo-guided-narrow.png` | 390px guided sample without horizontal overflow |
| `tests/visual/snapshots/demo-presentation-wide.png` | 90-second presentation mode |
| `tests/visual/snapshots/run-inspector.png` | Activity & results at the check beat, including sample PASS and live `NOT_RUN` (filename retained for history) |
| `tests/visual/snapshots/recovery-unknown.png` | Unknown native run and reconcile action |
| `tests/visual/snapshots/landing-wide.png` | Rewritten landing page with one primary CTA and the bespoke hero |
| `tests/visual/snapshots/landing-narrow.png` | Narrow landing page |
| `tests/visual/snapshots/workshop-wide.png` | Live workshop structure |
| `tests/visual/snapshots/onboarding-wide.png` | OpenCode connection/discovery |
| `tests/visual/snapshots/spirit-*.png` | Character states |

Video rules:

- Keep the recorded-sample label and `NOT_RUN` visible when showing evidence.
- Do not speed-edit the sample into a live run.
- Do not add fake terminal output, dashboards, success badges, or deployment results.
- If a live recording fails, show the failure and say so.
- Use the actual viewport; do not stretch narrow screenshots.

## Regenerating snapshots

```bash
npm run build
npm run test:visual
```

After a deliberate visual change:

```bash
npx playwright test --update-snapshots
```

Review every changed image before committing. A snapshot change is a UI decision, not an automatic approval.

## Clean exit

The guided sample ends with two honest exits:

- **Run locally** → `/workshop`, which shows the real connection/discovery flow.
- **Local setup** → `/#local-setup`, which links to the tested commands in `docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md`.

The hosted sample also rejects mutation routes, so “Run locally” is an explicit path to a local or private deployment rather than an implied capability of the public sample.

# Product brief — Unfinished Business

**Status:** Approved product; Upgrade Phase 5 (focused workshop and reorganized OpenCode controls) verified locally.
**Owner:** Product/interface.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01.

## One sentence

Unfinished Business is an OpenCode-powered hackathon project builder where four friendly spirits guide one unfinished idea through a clear proposal, an approved plan, a bounded real build, and evidence you can defend.

## Positioning

Unfinished Business is a **workshop around OpenCode**, not a replacement coding agent. OpenCode owns the model route, agent loop, native tools, tool permissions, execution, interruption, and native sessions. This product owns the four-stage workshop, exact-version approvals, dependency invalidation, evidence views, the first-run connection/discovery flow, and the Ghostlight interface.

The product is for a builder with an idea but no finished submission: a student at a hackathon, a solo maker on a short deadline, or a developer returning to a stalled project. It is not a multi-user platform, a hosted remote-code-execution service, or an autonomous deployer.

### Promise

- Make the next honest action obvious.
- Never turn a model reply into an approval.
- Never turn an unobserved result into evidence.
- Keep failures and empty states visible.
- Let a visitor understand the product before connecting an engine.

### Non-goals

- Remote access to a visitor's local repository.
- A public hosted sandbox with arbitrary execution.
- A second coding harness, inference client, or command executor.
- Silent paid-model fallback, fabricated usage metrics, testimonials, awards, or guaranteed outcomes.
- Automatic deployment, publication, or submission.

## Release truth (Phase 9)

The release candidate has one project story with three deployment modes:

| Mode | Browser can configure OpenCode? | OpenCode process | Persistence | Intended use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `local` | Yes; password may be held in memory | Supplies it separately on loopback | `UB_DATA_DIR` | A developer on their own Linux machine |
| `private-hosted` | No; environment/secret store owns the URL and password | Loopback child process | Private persistent disk | Protected Render or self-hosted instance |
| `hosted-demo` | No | None | None for visitors | Public deterministic sample |

Maker edits only the isolated demo workspace under `UB_DATA_DIR`. The product does not mount an arbitrary local or hosted repository in this release. The Node check is a bounded child process, not an OS sandbox. App approvals constrain workflow transitions; they never override an OpenCode permission denial.

## The four roles

| Spirit | Stage | Function | Approval boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oracle | Clarify | Turn an unfinished idea into a product proposal and open questions | The user approves the product; the proposal alone is not approval |
| Architect | Plan | Draft one planning section against its dependencies | The user approves the exact current version and hash; revisions make old approval stale |
| Maker | Build | Perform a bounded native edit through OpenCode | A separate Maker scope is required; OpenCode still owns tool permission |
| Witness | Review | Inspect evidence in a fresh session and prepare review drafts | Notes are drafts, not a submitted article, video, or proof of success |

### Workshop interface promise

The workshop shows one primary task at a time. The project outline opens as a drawer, Activity & results appears only when there is an operation or check, and Project memory holds decisions, answers, assumptions, constraints, and unresolved questions. Model and permission controls are visible; native IDs, capability mappings, raw evidence, provider payloads, sessions, revert controls, export, and transcripts stay under Technical details or Advanced diagnostics. A correction to Project memory supersedes the prior entry and never changes an approval or draft.

## Three honest usage paths

| Path | What it is | What it is not |
|---|---|---|
| Hosted demo | A labeled deterministic walkthrough served without OpenCode, credentials, a session token, or visitor persistence | Not live inference; not a sandbox; not access to a visitor's repository |
| Private hosted | A password-protected workshop on a private disk with a loopback OpenCode child | Not a public sandbox; not access to a visitor's local checkout |
| Full local mode | The browser app, local API, and pinned OpenCode server on the builder's machine over loopback | Not a guarantee of free-model availability; not permission to widen tool scope |

The landing page must describe all three without implying that a hosted page can read a local checkout. The hosted demo's `/workshop` route explains that it is read-only and offers the guided example or local setup as exits.

## OpenCode-only claim

Approved language:

> OpenCode supplies the agent loop, model access, native tools, permissions, and sessions. Unfinished Business adds the four-stage workshop, exact-version approvals, dependency invalidation, an evidence ledger, and a first-run connection/discovery panel.

Models are discovered from the OpenCode catalog rather than assumed. New projects may use any model OpenCode reports as available, with an optional free/local-only policy and an optional spending limit. A paid or unknown-price remote route requires an explicit confirmation before its first request; the app never silently substitutes a model or treats a model reply as approval. The free `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` route remains one reported option when available, but availability is time-limited and account-dependent.

Provider API keys stay in OpenCode. The first-run panel accepts only the OpenCode server Basic-auth password, holds it in memory for local work, and never exposes a provider-key field.

## Landing information architecture

1. Hero: “Turn unfinished ideas into hackathon-ready builds.”
2. Value statement and OpenCode-only positioning.
3. Primary actions: try the example, watch the guided workflow, run live with OpenCode, set up locally.
4. Three ways to use it: hosted demo, private hosted, and full local.
5. Four-spirit workflow explanation.
6. Deterministic demo teaser with an explicit fixture label.
7. OpenCode controls and evidence preview.
8. Idea-to-tool recommendation preview.
9. Local setup command tabs sourced from tested documentation.
10. Privacy and security boundaries.
11. FAQ and final call to action.

## The guided demo's role

The deterministic example is the product's **onboarding proof** and the judge's **fast path to the value story**:

- **Onboarding:** a first-time visitor can complete the whole journey — unfinished idea → approved plan → bounded implementation → diff/tests → Witness evidence → next step — without an OpenCode account, provider key, model quota, or repository.
- **Judging:** the same interface contracts render live and fixture runs, so the demo demonstrates the approval, permission, progress, evidence, and recovery surfaces without pretending the fixture is a live session.
- **Trust:** the demo is explicit about what it cannot prove. The live native session remains `NOT_RUN`; reset affects only the fixture; the hosted demo cannot mutate anything.

The demo is a **guided example**, not a second product surface. It uses the production `RunInspector`, `SpiritCharacter`, `SpiritStageTabs`, `StatusChip`, and shared workflow schemas.

## Calls to action

| Action | Destination | Truthful expectation |
|---|---|---|
| Try the example | `/demo` | An interactive, scripted fixture; not live inference |
| Watch the guided workflow | `/demo?presentation=1` | A 90-second screen-recording path over the same fixture |
| Run live with OpenCode | `/workshop` | The real workflow; engine status is visible and may be unreachable |
| Connect OpenCode | Setup dialog | Instructions only; no connection is implied until the engine answers |
| Set up locally | `#local-setup` | Commands match `docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md` |
| Walk through the fixture | `/demo` | Representative states with fixture IDs |

## Prohibited claims

Do not add:

- testimonials, customer logos, star ratings, or “trusted by” statements;
- user counts, build counts, time-saved figures, or success rates without a measured source;
- awards, rankings, organizer endorsements, or partner claims not actually granted;
- “guaranteed working build,” “autonomous,” “fully hosted coding agent,” or “reads your repository”;
- live-inference language around the deterministic demo;
- claims that app approval overrides an OpenCode permission denial.

## Success criteria

A first-time visitor can explain:

1. what the product does;
2. who Oracle, Architect, Maker, and Witness are;
3. OpenCode's role and the no-second-harness boundary;
4. the difference between the deterministic demo, a hosted/private instance, and full local mode;
5. what the product cannot reach.

## 8. Demo fixture boundaries

The guided sample is a browser-bundled fixture, not a server response and not a parallel UI. The same fixture also feeds the landing preview, visual snapshots, and the sample evidence view; `src/web/content/landing.ts` holds copy and configuration only, with no second operation/evidence state.

```text
src/shared/workflow.ts   production Zod schemas + types
        │
        ├─ src/server/workflow/model.ts  hashing, migration, persistence helpers
        ├─ src/shared/demo.ts            versioned fixture + beats + landing preview
        ├─ src/web/demo/DemoPage.tsx     playback + shared components
        └─ src/web/landing/DemoTeaser.tsx landing preview from the same fixture
                    │
                    ├─ RunInspector
                    ├─ SpiritStageTabs (inspect variant)
                    ├─ SpiritCharacter / StatusChip / Brand
                    └─ pure playback reducer (no API calls)
```

`src/shared/demo.ts` has no `node:`, `fetch`, `process.env`, `Date.now`, or `Math.random`. Tests parse the fixture with the production schemas, recompute section hashes, and assert that the landing preview and guided sample report the same check and live-proof status. Every recorded result is labeled; the live session remains `NOT_RUN`.

In `hosted-demo` mode the server independently returns the fixture from `/api/project` and `/api/export`, returns a read-only connection status, rejects `/api/session` and every non-GET `/api/*` request, and never constructs an OpenCode connection.

## 9. Trust boundaries and residual risks

## 9. Phase 9 release copy and boundary states

- Local mode copy says Maker edits the isolated demo workspace, not an arbitrary repository. The mode descriptor no longer claims workspace selection.
- Hosted-demo copy says there is no OpenCode, provider, session token, visitor persistence, or repository. `/workshop` is a read-only notice with exits to `/demo` and local setup.
- Private-hosted copy says the URL, password, and secrets are environment-managed; the browser cannot edit them.
- API copy distinguishes invalid session token, invalid origin, rate limit, concurrent mutation, request too large, stale revision, unknown native outcome, pending permission, and corrupt/busy state.
- Recommendation previews carry source and `verifiedAt` metadata. They describe only current capabilities and never imply an install, paid model, arbitrary shell, or approval.
- Evidence and Activity & results labels keep fixture results separate from live `NOT_RUN`/native results. No color or animation is the only status signal.
- The final accessibility matrix covers keyboard focus, dialog Escape, setup-tab arrow keys, 200% text zoom, 390px/wide layouts, overflow, reduced motion, contrast, and relevant screen-reader/live-region semantics.
